### 15w33c

- Protocol version 57
- Changed entity metadata format from a single byte for both type and index to several bytes:

  | Name | Type | Meaning |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | Index | Unsigned Byte | Unique index key determining the meaning of the following value, see the table below. If this is `0xff` then the it is the end of the Entity Metadata array and no more is read. |
  | Type | Optional Byte Enum | Only if Index is not `0xff`; the type of the index, see the table below |
  | Value | Optional *value of Type* | Only if Index is not `0xff`: the value of the metadata field |
- Remapped metadata types. These types match the final version except that BlockID is missing.

  | Value of Type field | [Type](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Data_types "Data types") of Value field | Notes |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | 0 | Byte |  |
  | 1 | VarInt |  |
  | 2 | Float |  |
  | 3 | String |  |
  | 4 | [Chat](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Chat "Chat") |  |
  | 5 | [Slot](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Slot "Slot") |  |
  | 6 | Boolean |  |
  | 7 | Rotation | 3 floats: rotation on x, rotation on y, rotation on z |
  | 8 | [Position](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Data_Types?action=edit&redlink=1 "Data Types (page does not exist)") |  |
  | 9 | OptPosition (Boolean + Optional Position) | Position is present if the Boolean is set to true |
  | 10 | Direction (VarInt) | ??? |
  | 11 | OptUUID (Boolean + Optional UUID) | UUID is present if the Boolean is set to true |

### 2011-9-29

- Beta 1.9 pre2.
- Protocol version is now 19
- Four packets changed:
  - [0x0F player block placement](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Protocol#Player_Block_Placement_.280x0F.29 "Protocol")
  - [0x66 window click](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Protocol#Window_click_.280x66.29 "Protocol")
  - [0x67 set slot](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Protocol#Set_slot_.280x67.29 "Protocol")
  - [0x68 window items](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Protocol#Window_items_.280x68.29 "Protocol")
- The change affects the "slot" datatype. This type consists of at least a short (item\_id). If this id isn't `-1`, a byte (count) and a short (uses) follow.
- From 1.9pre2 onward, additional data is sent but only for [certain item\_ids](https://gist.github.com/1268479). This means the protocol is no longer context free. The additional data is *at least* a short. If this short isn't -1, a byte[] array follows, containing *gzipped* NBT data
- The format of the NBT is as follows

```` ```
 COMPOUND
   LIST: 'ench'
     SHORT: 'id'
     SHORT: 'lvl'
   END
 END
``` ````

- So far only this format, with 'id' and 'lvl' set to `2` and `1` respectively, has been seen.
